quote: I'm reaching out here about the solar form you filled out online.
stewart_read: The intro references the form but gives no state/credibility anchor beyond that before the customer challenges the call's purpose seconds later.
coaching_implication: A stronger legitimacy anchor (company identity + why calling + brief value line) up front may have reduced the immediate 'what is this about' pushback.

quote: I I wanted some information, but I wanted a written information, not verbal conversations.
stewart_read: This is the send-proposal-before-meeting hard rule trigger; rep should hold the line with the canonical reasoning that proposals require explanation, but instead argues procedure ('you're jumping ahead too far').
alternative_hypothesis: Rep intended to eventually pivot to verify questions once she calmed the customer, but never got there.
coaching_implication: Use the canonical rebuttal: acknowledge the request, explain proposals need walkthrough to avoid confusion, and ask for the small set of details needed.

quote: that's why I'm asking you to send me information via US mail
stewart_read: Second touch of the same objection; rep cites 'we don't send quotes' but doesn't deliver the full canonical response (proposals need explanation) or ask a single qualifying question to keep momentum.
coaching_implication: Deploy the full hard-rule rebuttal verbatim-in-spirit: explain why proposals require a live walkthrough, not just 'we don't do that.'

quote: part of the process is we have to make sure I think I explained to you what I would like
stewart_read: Third touch — customer restates the boundary, rep restates the same design-process line instead of trying a genuinely different angle (small-ask, curiosity, or one qualifying question).
coaching_implication: This is where a pattern-interrupt or single very-low-commitment ask ('just your zip code and roof type, 30 seconds') could have kept the door open instead of a third repeat.

quote: so I'll just take you off my list
stewart_read: Rep concedes after essentially one sustained objection (repeated) rather than the target 3+ distinct angles; call ends with zero verify items captured.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: customer's tone ('I don't wanna be rude, but I think I'm making myself fairly clear') suggested a hard stop was near, so ending gracefully may have preserved the lead for a future touch rather than pushing into hostility.
coaching_implication: Even if disengaging, close with a bridge for future contact (e.g., 'I'll note that and have someone follow up with written details') rather than a flat list removal.

quote: And the system is custom made. It's not just a a cookie cutter type thing. Right?
stewart_read: Rep begins explaining product customization logic — closer-tier content — instead of redirecting to the specialist or simply asking the next qualifying question.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch: 'that's exactly what our specialist walks through — let's get the basics down first.'
